title: Five lessons from JCE Co-op’s rural broadband expansion
summary: Closing the rural digital divide requires long-term vision, local commitment and technology that can scale. Here’s what JCE Co-op’s expansion across northwest Illinois can teach other providers.
body_markdown:
JCE Co-op recently hit a major milestone in its fiber expansion. Its network now spans more than 3,000 route miles and serves more than 11,000 subscribers, with plans to pass nearly 30,000 homes, farms, businesses and community institutions over the next few years.


But the number that may say the most about the project is 19. That’s how many municipalities, lake associations and counties JCE honored through its Connected Community Awards program, recognizing areas where fiber buildout is complete or well advanced.


For providers tackling rural connectivity gaps of their own, JCE’s progress offers some useful lessons in strategic planning, workforce development, network operations, scalability and driving value after buildout.


**Lesson one: Think regionally, not project by project**


JCE has approached its expansion as a regional infrastructure strategy rather than a series of isolated fiber builds. Its planning considers how the network can support broadband subscribers, electric utility operations and additional revenue opportunities such as mobile backhaul.


Delivering that strategy has required investment from several sources. To date, it’s secured 14 broadband grants, including 11 from the State of Illinois and three federal awards.


Connect Illinois grants are supporting fiber connectivity to around 5,500 homes, businesses, farms and community anchor institutions across three counties. Two USDA Community Connect awards and one USDA ReConnect award support roughly 3,000 additional rural locations.


Local investment has also played an important role. Whiteside County committed $3 million in American Rescue Plan Act matching funds toward broadband development. Bringing those funding streams together has enabled JCE to build across multiple communities rather than treating each project as a standalone deployment.


**Lesson two: Invest in skills as well as infrastructure**


More fiber means more people are needed to build, maintain and develop it. JCE partnered with Morrison Tech, BEST Inc. and the State of Illinois to launch Illinois’ first fiber technician apprenticeship program, using the Fiber Broadband Association’s OpTIC Path curriculum.


That program connects broadband investment directly with workforce development, creating local career opportunities while building the skills needed to support advanced communications infrastructure for years to come. For rural providers, investing in people can be just as important as investing in technology.


> JCE has approached its expansion as a regional infrastructure strategy rather than a series of isolated fiber builds.


**Lesson three: Design for the realities of rural operations**


Building a broadband network is one challenge. Operating it efficiently across thousands of route miles is another. Across a footprint that large, sending technicians into the field solely to locate a fault can quickly become expensive and time-consuming, particularly during severe weather or when access is difficult.


Our ALM fiber monitoring platform helps JCE pinpoint issues remotely, accelerate response times and reduce unnecessary truck rolls across low-density service areas. JCE also uses our Intellifi™ managed Wi-Fi solution, giving the provider greater visibility into the subscriber experience while giving customers more control over their home connectivity. One improves visibility across the network itself. The other helps ensure a better experience at the edge of it.


**Lesson four: Build for the demand you don’t know about yet**


Public funding creates an opportunity to extend fiber into areas that have traditionally been difficult to serve. The technology decisions made during that buildout will shape how easily providers can add capacity, introduce new services and respond to changing customer needs in the years ahead, especially when funding landscapes change.


Working closely with JCE Co-op, we’ve provided the software-driven fiber access platform behind its expansion. With an open architecture, JCE has the flexibility to add capacity, introduce new services and adapt to changing customer requirements without disruptive upgrades.


**Lesson five: Buildout is the start, not the finish line**


JCE’s Connected Community Awards recognized 13 municipalities, three lake associations and three counties across northwest Illinois. With fiber buildout complete or well advanced across these communities, attention turns towards customer experience, ongoing network performance and the long-term value the network delivers.


Expanding broadband availability is critical, but the true measure of success is adoption. Communities realize the greatest return on broadband investments when residents and businesses understand the advantages of fiber, trust its reliability and integrate it into their daily lives and operations. Adoption rates, service quality and customer satisfaction help reveal whether network availability is translating into sustained economic growth, innovation and opportunity.


Greater adoption opens the door to the applications the network was built to support. For farms, that can mean precision agriculture and automated livestock monitoring. Businesses can access new digital tools and opportunities. Families gain easier access to telehealth, education and remote work. Communities can become more attractive places to invest, grow and build careers.


**The real measure comes next**


JCE’s experience offers a useful model for providers planning rural broadband expansion, from long-term thinking and workforce development to operational efficiency and building networks that can scale as demand grows.


Thousands more homes, farms, businesses and community institutions remain within JCE’s planned expansion, while many connected communities are already beginning to realize the benefits of reliable, high-speed broadband.


As deployment progresses, the focus naturally shifts towards adoption, service quality and the overall customer experience.


For providers pursuing broadband expansion of their own, JCE’s journey highlights the importance of looking beyond construction targets and preparing for the realities that come after buildout. The next chapter is about helping communities make full use of the connectivity now available to them while continuing to optimize operations, build long-term confidence in the service and strengthen trust in the brand.
